I have skills in Python, Machine Learning/AI and data analysis and I love to take NASA’s open Earth and space data and turn it into practical real-world solutions. Looking for motivated team mates with web/app dev, UI/UX, research or presentation skills. Join me to learn, innovate and build a strong NASA Space Apps Challenge solution together!
summary: AstroCare Pro is an offline-capable astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for long-duration space missions. It integrates physiological, behavioral, and environmental health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, sleep, exercise, hydration, radiation exposure, mood, and stress, into a unified dashboard. The platform assesses the five major NASA spaceflight hazards, tracks health trends, and provides AI-powered bone-loss risk predictions with explainable contributing factors and recommendations. Supporting compatible Bluetooth medical sensors and simulated readings, it enables health monitoring in connectivity-limited environments where communication delays with Earth can reach 22 minutes one-way. PDF, CSV, and JSON exports facilitate medical reporting and review. AstroCare Pro aims to improve astronaut health awareness and support informed decision-making during deep-space exploration. It is a research prototype, not a certified medical device.
details:
AstroCare Pro – Project Overview

AstroCare Pro is an innovative, offline-capable astronaut health monitoring and decision-support web application designed to tackle the medical and operational challenges faced during long-duration space exploration. This project empowers astronauts to autonomously monitor their health, identify potential risks, and access vital health insights, especially during deep-space missions where communication with Earth may be limited.

Functionality

The application features a comprehensive health monitoring dashboard that aggregates and displays a wide range of physiological, behavioral, and environmental health data. Users can log various health metrics, including:

  • Heart rate
  • Blood pressure
  • Oxygen saturation (SpO₂)
  • Body temperature
  • Sleep duration
  • Exercise levels
  • Hydration status
  • Body weight
  • Radiation exposure
  • Mood and stress levels
  • Social connections
  • Cabin CO₂ levels
  • Noise levels
  • Extravehicular activity (EVA) duration

AstroCare Pro analyzes this data to calculate health indicators, detect unusual readings, and generate color-coded alerts with suggested countermeasures. By utilizing historical health records, the application helps users track trends and understand changes in their health over time.

AI-Driven Health Insights

A standout feature of AstroCare Pro is its AI-powered bone-loss risk prediction module. This tool assesses health and mission-related data to estimate potential bone-loss rates, providing insights into contributing factors, risk categories, and actionable recommendations. The integration of TensorFlow.js enables machine-learning capabilities, with an offline prediction fallback for environments lacking external connectivity.

The platform also evaluates the five major NASA Human Research Program (HRP) spaceflight hazards:

  • Space radiation
  • Isolation and confinement
  • Distance from Earth
  • Altered gravity
  • Closed environment

Each assessment incorporates available health and environmental data, presenting risk scores, contributing factors, NASA-related references, and potential countermeasures.

Hardware and Sensor Integration

AstroCare Pro utilizes Web Bluetooth technology to connect with compatible medical devices and retrieve health measurements. Supported Bluetooth sensor categories include

  • Heart-rate monitors
  • Blood-pressure monitors
  • Pulse oximeters
  • Thermometers
  • Weight scales

The application also features smartwatch and device discovery capabilities. For development, testing, and demonstrations, simulated sensor readings are provided when physical hardware is unavailable, with automatic sensor logging to transfer collected data into health records.

Development Technologies

AstroCare Pro is built using:

  • HTML5: For application structure and interface components.
  • CSS3: To create responsive layouts, dashboard styling, animations, and visualizations.
  • JavaScript: For application logic, health calculations, data processing, alerts, and interactivity.
  • TensorFlow.js: For machine-learning integration in bone-loss prediction.
  • Web Bluetooth API: To communicate with compatible medical sensors.
  • NASA DONKI API: For accessing space-weather events and radiation-related information.
  • LocalStorage: To ensure local persistence of astronaut profiles, health records, and application settings.

The application features a responsive dark-themed interface suitable for both desktop and smaller screens, incorporating accessibility features, multilingual support, and interactive dashboard navigation.

Impact and Benefits

AstroCare Pro significantly reduces reliance on continuous Earth-based medical assistance by providing astronauts with locally accessible health information and automated risk assessments. Its unified dashboard enhances health awareness, while historical trends, alerts, and explainable predictions facilitate informed decision-making.

Moreover, the project investigates how space-health research can enhance healthcare and safety on Earth, particularly in remote environments, isolated research stations, and scenarios where immediate medical support is not readily available.

Innovation and Creativity

AstroCare Pro's innovation lies in its integration of astronaut health monitoring, NASA HRP hazard assessment, Bluetooth sensor connectivity, AI-driven bone-loss prediction, space-weather information, and offline-capable operation within a single browser-based platform.

AstroCare Pro is dedicated to making autonomous health monitoring a vital aspect of safer, more sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.

Disclaimer: AstroCare Pro is a research and decision-support prototype, not a certified medical device. Its predictions and assessments are not medical diagnoses and do not substitute for professional medical judgment.
